geometry._trackwidth_note: trackwidth is the CALIPER-MEASURED wheel separation (stakeholder, 128 mm). Do NOT bend it to make turns land -- it is the one independently verifiable number in this file. Scrub correction belongs in calibration.rotational_slip; main.cpp derives an effective track = trackwidth / rotational_slip and hands THAT to Drive/Odometry/plannerLimits.

calibration._otos_linear_scale_note: 2026-07-30 (126-003), camera-measured on the playfield, robot tethered. 18 straight-line runs (lengths 150/300/350mm, both directions, 3 reps each, ping-ponged to stay field-safe), OTOS delta (already scaled by the then-committed 1.067) vs. camera-measured travel at rest before/after each leg. Fit OTOS_mm = slope * camera_mm through the origin: slope=1.0384 (OTOS reads consistently long). Residual against the OLD 1.067 value: mean +3.91% sd 0.79% (95% CI [+3.55%,+4.27%], n=18) -- excludes 0, so 1.067 was wrong, not just noisy. Corrected = old_committed x (1/slope) = 1.067 x 0.9630 = 1.0275. A prior 12-run pilot set (lengths 150/300mm only, before repositioning for the 350mm block) gave a consistent 1.0330 -- both land in the same ~1.03 neighborhood, not the committed 1.067. Reflashed (mbdeploy, gen_boot_config.py regenerated boot_config.cpp's linearScale=1.0275f) and re-verified with a 6-run post-reflash spot-check (300mm, both directions, 3 reps): residual collapsed to mean +0.37% sd 0.34% (95% CI [+0.10%,+0.65%], n=6) -- an order of magnitude tighter than the pre-correction +3.91%, though still technically nonzero at this sample's precision (implied further correction ~1.0236, ~1mm on a 290mm leg). Not chasing that last fraction of a percent further -- it is at or below the camera measurement's own noise floor (a few mm of AprilTag pose jitter) and well past the point of diminishing returns for a boot-baked constant. Provenance of the original 1.067 is unknown (predates this sprint); this is the first camera-anchored measurement of it.
calibration._rotational_slip_note: 2026-07-29, camera-measured on the playfield. Scrub: the ratio of ACTUAL rotation to what ideal differential kinematics (omega = (vR-vL)/b) predict -- a skid-steer robot drags its wheels sideways through a turn and under-rotates. 180 deg in-place turns vs overhead AprilTag truth, 3 W->N->E / 3 E->N->W: 180.3 deg actual (sd 1.9), 100.2%. Equivalent to an effective track of 140.4 mm against the measured 128. Domain {0} u [0.5, 1.0] (config.proto); 0 is the uncalibrated sentinel meaning apply no correction. Consumed at BOOT (gen_boot_config.py -> boot_config.cpp -> main.cpp kEffectiveTrack); a runtime CONFIG rotSlip patch acks ERR_UNIMPLEMENTED, so changing it needs a reflash.
calibration._rotation_calibration_note: 2026-07-29, camera-measured, robot untethered. Turn response is affine: actual = gain*commanded + offset, fitted over 48 shuffled in-place turns (15/30/45/90/135/180 deg, both directions, omega 2.5/4.5/6.5/8.0 rad/s). The SAME law holds at every rate -- accuracy does not degrade with speed, so this is geometry/stiction, not a dynamics artifact. The ~-6 deg offset is why small turns were so bad: a 15 deg command landed at 9. Inverting it (commanded = (desired - offset)/gain) and re-running 47 trials gave a residual of mean +0.64 deg, sd 2.13, max 6.5 -- verified at 8.0 rad/s as well as 2.5. SIGN MAPPING, confirm before trusting: these were measured in the camera frame, where POSITIVE commanded omega DECREASES yaw. _pos here = positive commanded omega (clockwise in camera), _neg = negative. NOT YET CONSUMED BY FIRMWARE: rotation_gain_pos/neg and rotation_offset/neg exist in msg::DrivetrainConfig but have no reader and no emitter in gen_boot_config.py -- dead data, exactly as rotational_slip was before this session. Compensation is currently applied host-side (scratchpad turn_verify.py) because the robot is on battery and cannot be reflashed; wire it up next time it is on the bench.

control._shaper_note: decel-into-the-goal campaign (2026-07-22, follow-on to clasi/issues/angle-stop-overshoot-61-73-percent-on-hardware.md's own 'Option 1... remains the path to closing that residual further'): a_max/a_decel/j_max/yaw_jerk_max were dead data (orphaned by 115-003's motion-stack excision, gen_boot_config.py's own docstring documented them 'unread') until THIS campaign made them live again via Motion::VelocityShaper -- gen_boot_config.py's shaper_config_for_config() now reads all six of a_max/a_decel/alpha_max/alpha_decel/j_max/yaw_jerk_max into Config::ShaperBootConfig, consumed by App::MoveQueue to taper the commanded speed toward each Move's own stop threshold (a_max/a_decel/j_max/yaw_jerk_max source VALUES UNCHANGED, still 800.0/800.0mm/s^2 and 5000.0mm/s^3/100.0rad/s^3 -- carried forward, not retuned, since they were already reasonable bench starting points). alpha_max/alpha_decel are NEW this campaign (a_max/a_decel's angular sibling, no prior msg::PlannerConfig field to inherit from): alpha_decel=7.0rad/s^2 is derived from the taper-distance formula VelocityShaper itself implements (angle = omega^2/(2*alpha)) targeted at the ticket's own '15-20deg taper from omega=2rad/s (the TestGUI cruise rate)' bound -- 2^2/(2*7.0) = 0.2857rad = 16.4deg, inside that band. alpha_max mirrors alpha_decel (symmetric ramp-up/taper), matching a_max/a_decel's own symmetric 800.0/800.0 precedent. jerk-limited S-curve stage (same day, stakeholder correction): the shaper's own commanded ACCELERATION is now itself slewed by at most j_max/yaw_jerk_max per second (velocity_shaper.h's own file header has the full algorithm) -- j_max=5000mm/s^3 means a_max=800mm/s^2 is reached from rest in 0.16s; yaw_jerk_max=100rad/s^2 means alpha_max=7rad/s^2 is reached in 0.07s -- both plausible, not yet independently bench-retuned this campaign (carried forward from their pre-existing sprint-114 values).

control._vel_ki_note: kept 0.0018 in the 2026-07-11 session; motion_control.ipynb then showed the loop is FF-dominated with 40-50% step overshoot and weak steady-state correction -- a feedback-dominant retune (kp/ki up, acceptance via motion_control.ipynb) is the open next step.
control._vel_gains_note: 2026-07-15 RESONANCE TAMED (106-002, live config() gain sweep -- P4 binary wire, tests/bench/velocity_step_response.py, no reflash between trials): vel_kp 0.0014->0.0016, vel_kff 0.00135->0.0008. History: the ORIGINAL 0.0018 loop had a ~140 mm/s overshoot RESONANCE (+24..+33% on a velocity step); the 2026-07-12 interim detune (vel_kp 0.0018->0.0014, vel_ki 0.008->0.005, vel_kaw 15->20) only halved it (~+11%, still over the <~10% bar) and cost rise time. This session's own bench grid at kp=0.0014/kff=0.00135 measured worst-case +25% at 140mm/s (reproducing the historical pattern -- the interim detune alone did not clear the bar this session either). Root cause, found by exhausting kp/ki/kff/iMax/kaw per architecture-update.md (106) Decision 4: kff (feedforward) was OVER-estimated -- raising it (tried 0.0016) made overshoot WORSE (kff*target is an immediate open-loop kick added on top of kp*error, so an over-large kff over-drives the plant right at the step) -- confirming the 2026-07-11 kff derivation's own flagged 620-740mm/s measurement variance was real drift, not noise. Lowering kff to 0.0008 (with kp still at 0.0014) killed the resonance (worst 2.1%) but slowed rise time by ~30-50% (0.9-1.5s vs the interim's 0.9-1.28s) -- kp=0.0016 restores it: 3 consecutive full-grid confirmation runs all passed the <~10% bar with FASTER rise times than the interim detune (worst overshoot 9.3%/4.3%/5.0%; rise times 0.28-0.98s vs the interim's 0.9-1.5s) -- both overshoot AND rise time improved over the shipped interim, not just traded off. vel_ki/vel_kaw unchanged (0.005/20.0) -- the fix lived entirely in kp/kff, ki/kaw were not the lever needed this time. Re-verified from a clean reflash (boot defaults only, no live config() call) after persisting -- see 106-002's own completion notes for the full before/after table. Endpoint-accuracy re-verification (turn_sweep.py-style angle grid) NOT re-run this session -- flagged as a follow-up if endpoint regressions are observed, per the interim detune's own precedent of trading a little endpoint accuracy for trajectory smoothness. vel_filt=0.3 unchanged. See clasi/sprints/106-host-trajectory-planner-profiled-twists-straights-and-turns/issues/heading-loop-output-clamp-and-velocity-resonance.md's own Part 2 (marked resolved by 106-002) for the fuller history.
control._vel_filt_note: kept 0.3: raising to 0.6 (2026-07-11) cut measurement lag but pushed step overshoot to ~11% and turns to +6/+9/+7 -- the decel-lag surplus just became an overshoot surplus. 0.3 is the verified optimum of that trade with the current gains.
control._drive_limits_note: 2026-07-12 (sprint 100-001, motion-stack-v2 M1): starting values, not yet bench-tuned, for the new source/drive/ subsystem's Drive::Limits/tracker/policy tunables (PlannerConfig fields 15-31). v_wheel_max=620.0 is the one BENCH-MEASURED exception (mm/s plateau, matching the 2026-07-11 duty-saturated measurements already cited by _vel_kff_note -- NOT a starting guess). track_k_s/track_k_theta/track_k_cross/trim_v_max carry the issue's own Kanayama trim-law table verbatim (2.0/6.0/1.5e-5/120.0 -- track_k_theta=6.0 additionally matches heading_kp's own sprint-098 hardware-proven value, since both are the same physical outer-loop gain generalized). trim_omega_max=2.0 is the issue table's PIVOT-mode value ('1.0 arc / 2.0 pivot [rad/s]'); the lower arc-mode ceiling is left to the tracker's own per-mode logic (ticket 004), not a second wire field -- flagged. replan_err_pos=40.0/handoff_tol_pos=40.0 approximate BOTH the along-track envelope's flat term (40mm) and the cross-track bound (35mm/30mm respectively) with one shared value each -- flagged. handoff_tol_v=0.14 is the issue's flying-handoff formula's own velocity-coupling slope ('e_along <= 0.14*vExit + 40mm'), dimensionally a time constant despite the '_v' name -- flagged. steer_headroom=20.0/wheel_step_max=150.0 have no issue-table anchor at all; picked conservative placeholders (steer_headroom mirrors the old RobotConfig.steerHeadroom starting value; wheel_step_max is ~1.25x trim_v_max) -- flagged. replan_hold=0.2/replan_min_period=0.3/replan_max=3.0/replan_err_theta=0.15/arrive_vel_tol=15.0/arrive_dwell=0.15 are direct transcriptions of the issue's replan-envelope/terminal tables. See ticket 001's completion notes for the full field-by-field derivation; M11 (bench: arc_sweep grids) re-tunes all of these against the real plant.
control._drive_calibration_note: duty_per_speed_* [duty/(mm/s)]: open-loop wheel calibration, the inverse of the measured plant gain (speed_sweep 2026-07-27: L ~560, R ~510 mm/s per duty; ceiling ~500 mm/s). Per-wheel because the two gearboxes differ ~10%. crawl_pulse [-1,1]: fixed pulse amplitude for sub-breakaway wheel speeds, Bresenham-dithered in App::Drive; 0 disables. Measured breakaway is 1-6% duty and state-dependent (src/tests/firmware/duty_min/RESULTS.md) -- the earlier 0.20 was sized against a duty_sweep criterion that the standalone prober disproved, so crawl ships OFF pending a re-measure of the low end.
control._wheel_correction_note: wheel_gain_* / wheel_intercept_* [dimensionless, mm/s]: the measured commanded->actual line per wheel per direction of approach (measured = gain*commanded + intercept), from docs/design/wheel-speed-command-mapping.md. App::Drive inverts it: command = (desired - intercept)/gain. Measured against a SHARED duty_per_speed on both wheels -- recalibrate both wheels to one constant before re-characterizing, or the measurement inherits the mismatch. gain 1 / intercept 0 = no correction.
